summary:
Project ECHO (Earth Correlation and Habitat Observation) is a full-stack scientific decision-support platform that discovers, qualifies, and permits terrestrial analog sites for NASA's Artemis IV lunar South Pole surface campaign (2028).

Artemis IV astronauts will test rovers, drills, and spacesuits on crater rims where temperatures plunge to -246 degrees Celsius, slopes reach 25 degrees, and abrasive regolith contains corrosive sulfur. Before flight, engineers must rehearse on Earth, but existing analog catalogs are static and limited to a handful of well-known sites.

ECHO solves this through a 6-module pipeline:

1. An interactive 3D Moon globe built from NASA LRO LOLA and Diviner data.

2. A multi-objective ML matching engine (R-squared = 95.10%) that discovered 15 novel, unvisited candidate sites across Antarctica, Chile, and Iceland.

3. Deep-dive scientific dossiers.

4. A Google Gemini AI regulatory permit intelligence system.

5. A 3D digital twin hardware exposure lab with real sulfur degradation modeling.

6. An empirical validation dashboard with PDS-verified cross-validation.

All data is sourced from NASA PDS, Copernicus, ERA5-Land, and PetDB, with zero static placeholders and zero hallucinated permits.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

ECHO is a 6-module, end-to-end platform for qualifying terrestrial analog sites for NASA Artemis IV lunar South Pole hardware testing.

Module 1: Mission Brief

An interactive 3D WebGL globe of the lunar South Pole (80 to 90 degrees South), rendered from NASA LRO LOLA 240m altimetry and Diviner thermal radiometry. Users select from 4 verified Artemis IV candidate landing sites (Shackleton Rim, Malapert Massif, Haworth PSR, Connecting Ridge) with real-time grazing sun angle computation (+2.4 to +7.1 degrees).

Module 2: Discover Sites

A multi-objective machine learning matching engine compares 8 physical parameters (temperature extrema, slope, sulfur concentration, plagioclase mineralogy, aridity, elevation, FeO weight percent, and pyroxene content) between lunar targets and 30 global Earth candidate sites. The engine uses a Random Forest regressor trained on NASA PDS and Copernicus data with 5-fold spatial block cross-validation, achieving R-squared = 95.10% and RMSE = 0.0315. A "Novel / Unvisited Sites Only" filter highlights 15 newly identified locations with ZERO documented prior NASA field usage.

Module 3: Site Dossier

A deep-dive, 4-pillar scientific characterization for each candidate site, covering geological composition, thermal regime, terrain morphometry, and negative constraint analysis (where the analog breaks down relative to lunar conditions).

Module 4: Access and Permits

An AI-powered regulatory permit intelligence system using Google Gemini 2.5 Flash. It identifies all applicable permits, zoning laws, environmental clearances (NEPA), export controls (ITAR/EAR), and statutory restrictions (Wolf Amendment, P.L. 112-55, Section 539) for any candidate site worldwide. All AI-generated permit information is clearly flagged as advisory versus verified statutory data.

Module 5: Exposure Lab

A 3D digital twin hardware simulation environment where users import NASA CAD models (.glb, .gltf, .obj) of Artemis IV equipment (TX-DRILL coring mast, Lunar Terrain Vehicle, Regolith Robotic Arm, Cold-Soak Lander) and simulate sulfur-driven material degradation using an empirical wear model calibrated against plagioclase abrasion and sulfate corrosion data.

Module 6: Validation

An empirical ML validation dashboard showing actual-vs-predicted scatter plots, residual distribution histograms, 95% confidence interval envelopes, and 5-model benchmark comparisons, all powered by real PDS-verified data, not simulated or mock values.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

1. Discovers 15 novel, unvisited Earth analog sites that have never been used for NASA field testing, breaking the "legacy site bottleneck" of repeatedly relying on Devon Island, Arizona, and Hawaii.

2. Provides mission planners with quantified, auditable analog fidelity scores instead of qualitative "looks similar" assessments.

3. Automates the complex multi-jurisdictional statutory permitting process that currently takes weeks of manual legal research.

4. Enables hardware engineers to digitally stress-test rover components against realistic abrasive regolith chemistry before committing to expensive physical field prototypes.

5. All scientific claims carry full provenance citations traceable to NASA PDS4 product identifiers.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE

Frontend:

React 19, TypeScript 7, Vite 8.3

Three.js 0.187, react-three/fiber 9.4, and react-three/drei 10.7 (3D WebGL lunar and Earth globes, hardware digital twins)

Tailwind CSS 4.3 (responsive styling)

Recharts 3.10 (scientific scatter plots, histograms)

Lucide React (iconography)

Motion / Framer Motion (animations)

Bakend:

Python 3.14, Django 5.0, Django REST Framework 3.14

scikit-learn 1.3 (Random Forest, RobustScaler, spatial cross-validation)

NumPy 1.24, Pandas 2.0 (data processing)

xarray and h5netcdf (NetCDF4 multidimensional climate data)

External APIs:

Open-Meteo Archive API (historical climate verification)

Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) API (ERA5-Land soil temperature)

PetDB (EarthChem/IEDA) for whole-rock geochemical assays

Deployment:

Vercel (multi-service: Vite frontend and Django backend)

GitHub (version control, public repository)

CREATIVITY

ECHO is creative because it:

1. Treats analog selection as a MULTI-OBJECTIVE optimization problem across 8 coupled physical parameters simultaneously, not a single-variable lookup.

2. Introduces a "Novelty Filter" that deliberately surfaces sites with ZERO prior NASA usage, breaking decades of field testing bias toward the same handful of well-trodden locations.

3. Combines planetary science, machine learning, 3D hardware simulation, and legal regulatory intelligence into a single unified workflow that has never existed before as an integrated platform.

4. Uses a 3D digital twin approach where NASA engineers can import their own proprietary CAD hardware models and simulate surface exposure conditions.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Accessibility: A full-stack web application accessible via any modern browser with no installation, plugin, or registration required.

Cost: Uses exclusively open and free NASA and ESA datasets, with no paid data subscriptions. The Gemini API is available on a free tier.

Energy: Client-side WebGL rendering minimizes server-side computation. The ML model runs in milliseconds on standard hardware.

Scientific Integrity: Every data point carries provenance citations. The platform explicitly warns users that Earth analogs CANNOT reproduce lunar vacuum, 1/6th gravity, cosmic radiation, or electrostatic regolith levitation.
